title: Grateful Dead Live at Swing Auditorium on 1969-12-13
lineage: 7" Master Soundboard Reels > Cassette > DAT > CDR

ai_review.summary: Clear soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1969 set with a smoking Lovelight, standout Black Peter and China Cat > I Know You Rider jam, despite occasional sloppy moments.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean 1969 soundboard tape that presents the band’s lively performance well, though there is a brief static glitch at the end of Lovelight and a missing portion of Black Peter. Musically the show shines with a scorching Lovelight, tight transitions (St Stephen → Lovelight, China Cat → Rider) and strong renditions of Black Peter, Cumberland Blues, Good Lovin' and Hard to Handle. Overall the energy is high and the set is considered one of the better early‑year performances despite its short length.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating ~3.8, strong praise for musical highlights and generally good soundboard quality; weighting yields a solid 4‑star recommendation.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear 1969 soundboard with decent separation and low hiss; minor static glitch near the end of Lovelight and an incomplete Black Peter segment, but overall very listenable.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: Overall set length issues (missing Black Peter portion) – some listeners felt the show was a bit short and sloppy in spots.
show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong transitions, especially St. Stephen → Lovelight and a jammy China Cat into Rider; the flow feels cohesive despite the abbreviated runtime.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar on Lovelight 'smokes' and his vocals are described as heartfelt; mid‑song solo praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass lines highlighted as great, particularly during the China Cat jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ lick noted; keyboards called magical and essential to the vibe.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann was reportedly late but provides solid rhythmic drive throughout.
